key_insight: Video Streaming Thinking (VST) enables VideoLLMs to 'think while watching' by running a synchronized reasoning stream alongside streaming perception, achieving real-time logical reasoning with much lower response latency than naive test-time scaling.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between streaming perception and synchronized logical reasoning for online VideoLLMs: existing approaches either prioritize frame-level perception or incur high reasoning latency when scaled at test time.
method: Dual-stream design: maintain a fast streaming perception pipeline and a parallel, synchronized reasoning stream that incrementally processes perceptual outputs.
Thinking-while-watching mechanism: trigger and continue logical inference continuously as new frames arrive, enabling early and progressive answers rather than waiting for full-context buffering.
Latency-aware scheduling and lightweight incremental state (memory/prompts) to balance throughput, accuracy, and response-time constraints in real-time deployments.
impact: Enables practical, low-latency VideoLLM deployment for interactive, real-time applications (e.g., live QA, robotics, surveillance) by delivering synchronized reasoning without sacrificing responsiveness or model quality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two parallel streams: Streaming Perception -> Incremental Features, and Synchronized Reasoning -> Progressive Outputs
Timeline visualization comparing baseline (perceive-then-reason) latency vs VST's overlapping perceive+reason with earlier answers
Throughput vs Latency chart showing VST trade-off improvements over test-time scaling
Illustrative icons: camera frames flowing into a 'brain' module with early text outputs (to convey thinking-while-watching)
paper_title: Video Streaming Thinking: VideoLLMs Can Watch and Think Simultaneously
paper_authors: Yiran Guan, Liang Yin, Dingkang Liang, Jianzhong Ju, Zhenbo Luo
